plugins.name: coding-skills
plugins.description: Engineering skills for the bugs that pass code review and fail in production: write skew, coordinated omission, retry storms, index locality.

skills.name: algorithmic-complexity-attacks
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "is this regex safe", "what is ReDoS", "why does CPU spike on one request", "how do I safely accept uploads or XML", "is this parser safe against untrusted input", or is reviewing a regex over user input, handling compressed files, or responding to a ReDoS advisory.
skills.description_zh: 分析用户输入正则的ReDoS、单请求CPU峰值、上传压缩文件/XML或解析器的算法复杂度攻击风险，支持相关安全评审与公告响应。

skills.name: cache-stampede
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how do I stop a thundering herd", "why does load spike when a cache key expires", "how should I set cache TTLs", "how do I handle cache misses for keys that do not exist", or reports many identical origin requests after an expiry, a spike after a cache flush or deploy, or one key saturating a cache node. Covers cache-expiry herds specifically. For retry storms and load shedding use `retry-amplification`.
headings: 2. Penetration: misses that can never hit
4. Hot key: one key exceeds one node
skills.description_zh: 诊断缓存到期清空发布后的惊群、大量重复源请求、缺失键与热点节点，指导TTL和未命中处理；重试风暴及卸载用retry-amplification。

skills.name: clocks-and-time
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how do I measure elapsed time correctly", "why do timestamps disagree across servers", "how do I order events across machines", "should I use timestamptz", "why did the cron job run twice", or is handling time zones, DST, clock skew, or logical clocks. Covers wall-clock, monotonic, and logical clocks. For database transaction ordering use `isolation-anomalies`.
headings: Rule 1: never measure duration with the wall clock
Rule 2: NTP does not produce synchronized clocks
Rule 4: DST arithmetic is not addition
skills.description_zh: 处理墙钟、单调钟和逻辑钟，指导耗时测量、跨机时间事件排序、时区DST偏差及cron重复；数据库事务排序另用隔离异常技能。

skills.name: code-hotspots
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "where should we start refactoring", "which files are riskiest", "what is our tech debt priority", "which files always change together", "what is the bus factor", or asks to mine git history for code health signals. Combines change frequency with complexity to rank refactoring candidates.
skills.description_zh: 挖掘Git变更频率、复杂度、共同修改与人员依赖等代码健康信号，排序重构候选和技术债风险。

skills.name: connascence
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is this so tightly coupled", "how do I decouple these", "is this coupling acceptable across a module boundary", or when reviewing positional arguments, magic values, required call ordering, shared mutable state, or duplicated algorithms. Provides a taxonomy that names and ranks kinds of coupling precisely.
skills.description_zh: 以精确分类和强度评估耦合，检查位置参数、魔法值、调用顺序、共享可变状态与重复算法，并判断模块边界耦合或解耦方案。

skills.name: connection-pooling
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how many database connections should I use", "why is the database out of connections", "should I use PgBouncer", "what is transaction pooling", "why do prepared statements fail behind a pooler", or is configuring pool size, max_connections, RDS Proxy, or a serverless database workload. Covers database connections specifically. For general pool sizing math use `queueing-and-utilization`.
skills.description_zh: 配置数据库连接池数量及max_connections，诊断耗尽、PgBouncer事务池、预处理语句、RDS Proxy及无服务器负载；通用池容量数学用排队利用率技能。

skills.name: consistent-hashing
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how do I shard this data", "how do I add a node without rehashing everything", "what is consistent hashing", "should I use rendezvous hashing", "how do I fix a hot shard", or is designing key partitioning or cache sharding across a changing set of nodes. Covers distributing keys across nodes. For caching behavior of a single hot key use `cache-stampede`.
headings: bisect for the first position clockwise
Cost of pinning keys to nodes
skills.description_zh: 通过一致性或rendezvous哈希设计变化节点集的键分区与缓存分片，处理扩容重哈希或热点分片；单热点键缓存行为用cache-stampede。

skills.name: coordinated-omission
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is production latency worse than our load test", "is this benchmark trustworthy", "how do I aggregate p99 across servers", "which load testing tool should I use", or when writing or interpreting a load test whose p99 looks suspiciously good. Covers whether latency numbers are measured correctly. For reducing an accurately measured tail use `tail-latency`.
skills.description_zh: 检验负载测试是否漏记排队等待导致延迟过好，解释生产与测试p99差异、跨服务器分位聚合和工具选择；已正确测量的尾延迟优化另用tail-latency。

skills.name: cyclomatic-complexity
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how complex is this function", "count the branches", "find overly complex functions", "set a complexity threshold", "reduce cyclomatic complexity", or asks to interpret a complexity report from radon, ESLint, gocyclo, PMD, or lizard. Also applies when a function "has too many if statements" and needs simplifying.
skills.description_zh: 评估函数分支及圈复杂度、设置阈值、识别和简化复杂函数，解释radon、ESLint、gocyclo、PMD或lizard报告。

skills.name: database-queues
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how do I build a job queue in Postgres", "what is SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED", "why are jobs processed twice", "how do I publish an event and commit a row atomically", "what is the outbox pattern", or reports workers blocking each other polling a jobs table.
headings: Bloat is the real operational cost
When to use a broker instead

skills.name: dependency-confusion
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how do I secure our package supply chain", "what is dependency confusion", "how do I stop typosquatting", "is this package safe to install", "should I pin dependency hashes", or is configuring a private registry, lockfile policy, or CI credentials for package installs.
headings: Supply chain: dependency confusion and friends
.npmrc scoped to the private registry only

skills.name: expand-contract
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks to "rename a column without downtime", "drop a column safely", "add NOT NULL to a live table", "add an index in production", "change an API response shape", "change an event format", or asks how to run a zero-downtime migration. Provides the expand-migrate-contract sequence and per-operation recipes.
headings: Consumer habits that lower the cost

skills.name: floating-point
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is 0.1 + 0.2 not 0.3", "how do I compare floats", "what type should I use for money", "why is my total off by a cent", "why do sums drift", or reports NaN appearing unexpectedly, a test failing on a tiny difference, or results differing between machines.

skills.name: hyrums-law
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "is this a breaking change", "can I change this undocumented behavior", "why did an internal change break a consumer", "how do I stop people depending on this", or is changing observable behavior never promised in a contract, such as iteration order, error message text, timing, sort stability, ID format, or JSON key order.
headings: Primary defense: make unspecified behavior unstable

skills.name: index-design
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is my index not being used", "which columns should I index", "what order should the composite index columns be in", "should this be a covering index", "which indexes can I drop", or is choosing a primary key type or auditing unused and duplicate indexes. Covers designing and auditing indexes. For diagnosing a specific slow query use `query-plans`.

skills.name: isolation-anomalies
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "which isolation level do I need", "why did concurrent requests break this invariant", "should I use SELECT FOR UPDATE", "what is write skew", or reports a bug that only reproduces under concurrent traffic, a lost update from a read-modify-write, or confusion about REPEATABLE READ behavior across databases.

skills.name: keyset-pagination
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is deep pagination slow", "how do I replace OFFSET", "how do I build a cursor-based API", "why do users see duplicate or skipped rows while paging", or is writing a batch job, export, or backfill that pages through a large table.

skills.name: metamorphic-testing
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how do I test this when I do not know the expected output", "how do I test a search ranking or ML model", "what is the oracle problem", "how do I test a scientific computation or optimizer", or is testing code whose correct answer cannot be computed independently. Covers testing without a known correct answer. For judging whether existing tests are strong use `mutation-testing`.
headings: no oracle, but a relation holds

skills.name: module-depth
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "should I split this class", "is this abstraction worth it", "why does this change ripple through so many layers", "is this wrapper useful", or when reviewing a new interface, wrapper, or layer. Applies Ousterhout's deep-versus-shallow module test, including when Clean Code's small-functions advice does not apply. Covers whether an abstraction earns its interface. For where validation belongs use `parse-dont-validate`.

skills.name: mutation-testing
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "are our tests actually good", "is 100% coverage meaningful", "what is mutation testing", "how do I measure test quality", "which tests are worthless", or is setting a coverage target or reviewing a test suite that passes while bugs still ship. Covers whether existing assertions detect bugs. For testing code with no known correct output use `metamorphic-testing`.
headings: Why the survivors are the point

skills.name: mvcc-and-bloat
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is the table growing despite deletes", "why did queries get slower over time", "why is autovacuum not keeping up", "what is transaction ID wraparound", "what is idle in transaction", or reports Postgres table or index bloat, replication slot growth, or vacuum warnings.

skills.name: parse-dont-validate
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "where should validation live", "how do I stop re-checking this everywhere", "how do I make illegal states unrepresentable", or when reviewing non-null assertions, casts, or repeated checks deep in the code, or designing a DTO whose optional fields are only valid in certain combinations.
headings: Signs of validating where parsing belongs

skills.name: query-plans
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is this query slow", "read this EXPLAIN output", "why is the planner not using my index", "why is it fast in staging but slow in production", or shares an execution plan to interpret. Covers EXPLAIN ANALYZE, estimate-versus-actual rows, join strategies, and statistics problems. Covers diagnosing a plan. For choosing which indexes to create use `index-design`.

skills.name: queueing-and-utilization
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how big should this thread pool be", "what CPU target is safe", "why did latency spike without more traffic", "do we have headroom at 85% CPU", "how deep should this queue be", or asks to size a worker fleet, connection pool, or WIP limit. Covers sizing and utilization targets. For throughput that drops as workers are added use `universal-scalability-law`, and for database connections use `connection-pooling`.
headings: One shared pool beats many small pools

skills.name: retry-amplification
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "how should I configure retries", "why is the service still down after we fixed the cause", "where should retries live in the call chain", "what backoff should I use", "how do I shed load", or reports a retry storm, thundering herd, or a system that will not recover after restart. Covers retry-driven overload specifically. For herds caused by cache expiry use `cache-stampede`.
headings: 2. Use a retry budget, not a retry count

skills.name: start-here
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks a broad engineering question that could match several areas, asks "which skill covers this", "what skills are available", "where do I start", or describes a symptom without naming a technique. Routes a symptom to exactly one of the coding-skills skills. Load this only when no single skill clearly matches.

skills.name: tail-latency
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is p99 bad when p50 is fine", "how do I reduce tail latency", "should I use hedged requests", "how do I set timeouts for a fan-out", or when a request touches many services or shards and adding a service made latency worse than that service's own latency. Covers reducing tail latency. For whether the p99 number itself is trustworthy use `coordinated-omission`.

skills.name: unicode-pitfalls
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why is this string length wrong", "how do I truncate text safely", "why do these identical strings not match", "how do I compare text case-insensitively", "why does emoji break my column limit", or is handling normalization, encodings, grapheme clusters, or homoglyph attacks.

skills.name: universal-scalability-law
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "why does adding servers not help", "why did throughput drop when we scaled out", "how far can this scale", "why is a bigger thread pool slower", or wants to fit a scalability curve to load test data or predict a capacity ceiling. Covers throughput that peaks then declines. For sizing a pool to a target latency use `queueing-and-utilization`.
headings: Where this applies day to day

skills.name: write-amplification
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks "should I use an LSM or a B-tree", "why is disk usage far bigger than my data", "why do writes slow down as data grows", "how do I tune RocksDB compaction", "what is write amplification", or is choosing a storage engine or database for a given read/write mix.
headings: Write amplification and the RUM conjecture
Where B-tree write amplification comes from
Where LSM write amplification comes from
Related knobs that are the same tradeoff

commands.name: find-skill
commands.description: Find which coding skill applies to a problem, or list them all

description: Engineering skills for the bugs that pass code review and fail in production: write skew, coordinated omission, retry storms, index locality.
